fixes: P1 (hand-off motion, the main cheap-seam risk): the claim that 'the frame-30 state is what the player sees during the hand-off dissolve' was never checked, and the overlay code says otherwise. In game/intro_overlay_snippet.html, finish() sets intro.style.opacity='0' as soon as #status fades, which is right after callMain, at about menu frame 0-1. The 0.9 s CSS 'ease' dissolve therefore runs across frames 1-20, while the nameplates (Grandbois, Sablon, Hautecouronne) are still popping in larger and offset (qa/nameplates_popin_mf003_vs_mf030.png). Mid-dissolve this will show as a ghosted double nameplate shrinking into place, the exact glitch an art director catches in the last second of an intro. Fix in the overlay spec: after engine-ready, count 30 canvas rAF ticks (or about 600 ms on device) before starting the dissolve. 0.6 + 0.9 = 1.5 s still fits inside the 3 s tour hold. Then prove it: run the same deterministic-clock Playwright harness through the real overlay and capture 4-5 mid-dissolve frames. If the delay is refused, rebuild f1983 on the frame that matches the actual dissolve midpoint instead.

P2 (assets for the reading-order unmask and drypoint alignment, required by storyboard section 13 / row 31 / line 450 from this native capture): rects.json and report_*.json have no content geometry. Export, per bucket: (a) card_contents.png, a straight-alpha RGBA layer of the live card contents (live capture over the rebuilt blank, unpremultiplied); (b) per-element rects in base units and px for title_mark (with both ornament groups), subtitle line 1 and 2, the rule (y, x-extent, centre boss), each of the 5 buttons and the footer; (c) the measured title glyph baseline y and rule y. Without these the 'card writes itself in reading order' beat will fall back to a crude rectangular wipe or a flat cross-fade, and the S22/S25 drypoint ruling cannot be placed exactly under the live baseline and rule.

P3 (client presentation): on its own, f1983 reads as 'menu with the UI missing'. The largest, brightest and softest surface in the frame is an empty rectangle, and the client will judge it that way. Put a context strip on the review sheet: the S24 leaf landing (f1760), f1983, two mid-dissolve frames with the card unmasking in reading order, and the live menu. The client is approving a transition, not a poster. Also fill the empty bottom-right of review_sheet_f1983 with the 4:3 100 % corner crops; right now only the 16:9 seams are shown.

P4 (unlit/relit desk states for S22-S24): the *_unlit candle layers keep the sprite's baked flame glow. The wax top and rim stay warm and bright, as if still lit, so in the f1612-f1707 near-darkness an unlit candle will read as lit wherever the comp lifts it. Make a true unlit wax variant by removing the top-down warm subsurface gradient over roughly the top 15-20 % of the body, matched to the lower body's tone. Also clean the dark wick specks and the base notch out of candle_left_flame / candle_right_flame / table_edge_bottom_flame. They are visible at 4x on dark, and S22's grow-back puts the flame alone on a dark ground.
